blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
At the rise level, the real test of a finance partner is whether tax is considered at the moment decisions are actually made. A pricing conversation, a sourcing decision, a new office, a large reimbursement scheme, a partnership structure — each one has a tax dimension that quietly shapes its real cost and real margin.

The mistake most teams make is to keep tax as a back-office function that only speaks up when a deal is already final. A good finance partner is in the room earlier, asking simple questions: does this change the VAT position? does it affect our corporate tax base? does it create any unexpected withholding? The questions themselves do not require deep expertise. They only require the habit of asking them.

Therefore, the discipline is cultural, not technical. Teach the business to bring tax into the conversation early, and the number of expensive surprises drops sharply. Leave it to the tax team alone, and the surprises continue — quietly, every quarter.

items.q: According to the text, when should tax be considered?
options: At the moment decisions are actually made
Only once a deal is final
Only when the tax team requests it
items.why: "tax is considered at the moment decisions are actually made" — o teste do parceiro de finanças.

items.q: What kind of expertise do the three simple questions require?
options: No expertise — only the habit of asking them
items.why: "The questions themselves do not require deep expertise. They only require the habit of asking them."

items.q: According to the text, the discipline described is…
options: the responsibility of the legal team
items.why: "Therefore, the discipline is cultural, not technical."

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Every major decision has a tax dimension.
Tax should stay in the back office until a deal is done.
The right questions matter more than deep expertise.
items.why: Inferência: o texto todo argumenta contra deixar o tax como função de retaguarda que só fala no fim.

items.q: The phrase "quietly, every quarter" at the end suggests that…
options: the tax team always catches them in time
the surprises keep recurring unnoticed if nothing changes
the surprises are rare and dramatic
tax problems only appear once a year
items.why: Inferência: 'quietly, every quarter' indica um custo recorrente e discreto que persiste se o hábito não mudar.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conversando com o time comercial. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, we are rewriting this partnership structure from scratch — and honestly, we should not have to. Three weeks ago, when the commercial team first shaped the deal, one question would have changed everything: does this create any withholding?

Nobody asked it. The structure routes the payments through a jurisdiction that triggers a withholding tax we now cannot recover. On the numbers we have, that is a meaningful hit to the margin — money that simply leaves the business every time we invoice.

I want to be clear: this is not about blame, and it is not about technical brilliance. The people in that room did not need to be tax experts. They only needed the habit of asking three plain questions before signing anything. Does this change the VAT position? Does it touch our corporate tax base? Does it create any unexpected withholding?

Therefore, going forward, I am asking to be in the room while the deal is still being shaped, not after it is final. If we build that habit, the expensive surprises drop sharply. Leave tax to the last page, and I promise you we will be back here next quarter, rewriting another structure.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is James rewriting the partnership structure?
options: The commercial team asked him to cut costs
A missed question created a withholding tax the company cannot recover
The client changed the pricing at the last minute
The corporate tax rate went up
items.why: "one question would have changed everything: does this create any withholding?" — e agora não pode ser recuperada.

items.q: What kind of person did the team need to be, according to James?
options: People with the habit of asking three plain questions
items.why: "They only needed the habit of asking three plain questions before signing anything."

items.q: What is James asking for going forward?
options: To be in the room while the deal is still being shaped
To hire a dedicated tax specialist
To review deals only after they are final
items.why: "I am asking to be in the room while the deal is still being shaped, not after it is final."

items.q: When James says the withholding is "money that simply leaves the business every time we invoice," he implies the cost is…
items.why: Inferência: 'every time we invoice' mostra que é uma perda que se repete, não um custo único.

items.q: How would you best describe James's tone?
options: Firm about the problem but focused on building a habit, not on blame
items.why: Inferência: ele diz 'this is not about blame' e propõe um caminho — hábito cultural, não culpa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "A good finance partner is in the room while the deal is being shaped." A finance partner is…
options: the person who signs the invoices
someone from finance who works alongside the business on decisions
items.why: Finance partner = parceiro de finanças que atua junto ao negócio, não apenas na retaguarda.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Routing the payments through that country created an unexpected ___ we cannot recover."
items.why: Withholding = retenção (de imposto na fonte), o problema criado pela estrutura.

items.q: "Each decision has a tax dimension that shapes its real margin." A tax dimension is…
options: the tax aspect or angle of a decision
the size of the tax department
items.why: Tax dimension = dimensão fiscal: o ângulo tributário embutido em cada decisão.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Keeping tax as a ___ function means it only speaks up when the deal is final."
items.why: Back-office = retaguarda; o erro é deixar o tax só nessa função de bastidor.

items.q: "The tax angle quietly shapes the real cost of the deal." To shape here means to…
options: influence or determine the form of
items.why: To shape = moldar, influenciar a forma e o custo real da decisão.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas de finanças e negócios. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The CFO still has to sign off on the new partnership structure." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the three-question checklist across all commercial teams." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two managers pushed back on bringing tax into early meetings." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "The team agreed to ask the tax questions but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "Catching that withholding early would move the needle on our margin." This means it would…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer uma diferença perceptível.
